steps.action:
# Three Causes of World War I

## 1. The Alliance System
Europe was divided into two major blocs — the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) and the Triple Entente (France, Russia, Britain). These interlocking treaty obligations meant that a localized conflict could rapidly pull every major power into war, like a chain reaction. A dispute between Austria-Hungary and Serbia ultimately engulfed the entire continent within weeks.

## 2. Nationalism
Intense nationalist movements — particularly Slavic nationalism in the Balkans — created deep instability. Serbian nationalism directly threatened the multi-ethnic Austro-Hungarian Empire. The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo (June 1914) by Gavrilo Princip, a Bosnian Serb nationalist, was a direct product of this pressure. Broader nationalist rivalries among great powers over prestige and territory also fueled hostility.

## 3. Militarism
A prolonged arms race — especially the Anglo-German naval rivalry — had produced enormous standing armies and rigid war plans (such as Germany's Schlieffen Plan). Military establishments gained enormous political influence, and mobilization timetables were so inflexible that once the process started, diplomats had little room to de-escalate. The culture of militarism also made war seem acceptable, even desirable, to many leaders.

Together, these forces created a Europe that was essentially primed to explode — needing only a spark.
